content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: outage message, overtime on both queues and chat deflection. It is predicted to lift service level to 82.5% over 12:15-14:15 for ₹9,084.","why":"The spike is driven by card_declined calls from P1 incident INC-20261016-7996, the card gateway outage. Card_declined calls are running at 2.26x normal, and service level has fallen to 44.6%. If we do nothing, the window is predicted at 47.4%, with payments at 34.6% and a 14.8% abandon rate. R2 tackles the outage directly with a known-issue IVR message for card_declined callers. It adds overtime for 35 payments and 10 general agents, deflects 20% of selected status and enquiry calls to chat on both queues, and uses a shorter 30-minute break shift. Predicted results are 82.5% overall (payments 79.6%, general 87.9%), abandons down to 4.4%, and 91.8% for the rest of the day. It is the cheapest option that reaches the 80% target and breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["R1 also reaches target (80.5%) but costs more (₹9,720) and does slightly worse on service level (82.5%) and abandons (4.4% vs 5.3%).","P3 (₹3,600, 72.6%) and P4 (₹4,050, 73.9%) are much cheaper but miss the 80% target, leaving payments at about 70-72%.","The no-cost plans miss the target by a wide margin: P2 reaches 55.6% and P1 45.6%. P1 actually makes things worse by pulling agents from general.","R2 protects the general queue (87.9%) rather than borrowing from it. Payments is still just under 80% on its own at 79.6%.","It depends on enough agents accepting overtime and on customers taking up chat deflection."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptance and card_declined volume each interval. If the gateway incident runs past 14:00, extend the IVR outage message. If the incident is resolved early, cut overtime back to save cost."}
